summary.text: A 34-year-old woman with a history of Hashimoto's thyroiditis and bilateral high myopia developed left eye pain on ocular movement on May 6, 2023, followed by progressive visual acuity decline. By May 9 her visual impairment had reached peak severity with only light perception remaining. On admission the direct pupillary light reflex of the left eye was diminished while the indirect reflex was preserved.

Serum AQP4-IgG was present at titer 1:32 and MOG-IgG absent by fixed cell-based assay. CSF routine and biochemical analyses were normal with IL-6 2.00 pg/mL, oligoclonal bands were present in serum and CSF, MRI showed no abnormal findings, VEP latency was prolonged on the left, the left visual field showed defects in all quadrants, and RNFL showed bilateral thinning, worse on the left. NMOSD was diagnosed due to the positive AQP4-IgG.

Intravenous methylprednisolone was given in tapering doses; visual acuity improved only from light perception to finger-counting at 30 cm with corrected vision 0.02. She was subsequently referred for plasma exchange over five sessions, following which corrected acuity improved to 0.4. Maintenance mycophenolate mofetil with oral prednisone 10 mg once daily resulted in 12 months free from relapse.

She attended a preconception consultation on March 13, 2024. Live cell assay showed serum AQP4-IgG at 1:10 and MOG-IgG positive at 1:32, and mycophenolate mofetil was replaced by satralizumab. She conceived three months later, was seronegative for AQP4-IgG with MOG-IgG 1:100 on October 10, 2024, and delivered a healthy female infant at 38 weeks on April 7, 2025 without symptom recurrence or adverse events. At 5 months postpartum mother and child were in good condition without relapses.

article_limitations: Figure pixels are reviewed in the separate visual submission; values printed inside images (visual field, RNFL and antibody-titer plots) are pixel content and are not recorded as facts.
Figure 2 prints a fixed cell-based assay point dated 2023.12.3 and a 2024.3.13 point that the case text does not date; these are pixel content only.
The discussion states AQP4-IgG was the primary pathogenic driver and that the satralizumab strategy was justified; these author interpretations are not recorded as clinical facts.
The discussion calls the MOG-IgG titer stable at 1:32, which does not match the 1:100 result on October 10, 2024; kept as an ambiguous review-only observation.
Live cell assay results at the preconception consultation are not dated in their own sentence and carry no time.
Literature cases cited in the introduction and discussion are not patient facts.

Live-cell assay technique statements (antigen substrate, transfected-cell controls, IgG Fc-specific secondary antibody) are laboratory method descriptions, not patient findings; they are not recorded as separate items. The decision to use the live-cell assay for this case and all subsequent monitoring is kept as a completed monitoring care plan.
The improvement to finger-counting after methylprednisolone is not ordered after the final 125 mg step, because the source does not say when during the course it was observed.
